messages:
emma (Support): Hey team, escalating from a customer — they started getting embedding dim errors after we rolled a batching tweak yesterday. Error: "dimension_mismatch: expected 1536, got 512". Happening intermittently on the embeddings route.

jane (Customer): repro: POST /v1/embeddings with payload of 4 short texts. We used model "embed-redwood-1536-v1". Usually returns 1536 floats but sometimes client sees 512. Occurs ~1 in 10 requests. Request-id: r-8b6c2f9a.

emma (Support): Customer attached curl and response snippet: 
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d '{"model":"embed-redwood-1536-v1","input":["a","b","c","d"]}'
```
Response excerpt: 
```
{ "error": "dimension_mismatch", "message": "expected 1536, got 512", "request_id":"r-8b6c2f9a" }
```

sam (Eng Runtime): Thanks. First guess: a model-variant routing mishap where batched requests are being routed to the 512-dim small model (embed-redwood-512-v1) due to aggressive batching+fallback policy. Can you share the exact route they hit (team/key) and last 2 request_ids? Also whether they are on Dedicated or Hosted.

jane (Customer): It's hosted. Another request id: r-8b6d3a1c. Both hits same route /v1/embeddings. No explicit batch_size set.

mike (SRE): ops-bot, can you surface trace for r-8b6c2f9a? Looking for routing decision and model selection logs.

ops-bot: Trace created: https://observability.redwood.ai/trace/r-8b6c2f9a (span breakdown available). Routing: matched policy "cost-prefetch" -> selected candidate pool: embed-pool-us-east (contains embed-redwood-1536-v1, embed-redwood-512-v1). Fallback used? no.

sam (Eng Runtime): Interesting — the trace shows model selection = embed-redwood-1536-v1 but the downstream inference node reported model_variant=embed-redwood-512-v1 in logs. That indicates either (A) a stale model symlink on the node or (B) an in-flight model swap where a node had the 512 weights loaded when the router thought 1536 was loaded.

emma (Support): Customer also reported higher tail latency when this started. They said p99 jumped from ~120ms to ~420ms. They suspected batching, but their per-request times vary. Any quick per-request latency breakdown we can share?

sam (Eng Runtime): We can provide a standard breakdown: queue_wait + model_load + compute + postproc + network. For embeddings specifically, model_load should be ~0ms if warm. From the trace: 
- queue_wait: 18ms
- model_load: 0-210ms (spikes when swapping)
- compute: 85-110ms
- postproc: 6ms
- egress/network: 12ms
When the bad dim happened, model_load was 170-210ms and compute matched 512-dim runtime.

mike (SRE): Repro steps we used in staging: send 4 inputs in one request, vary concurrency, and tail nodes' loaded model via: 
```
# on runtime node
curl http://localhost:9000/status | jq '.models_loaded'
```
We saw occasional mismatches during rolling deploys. Suggestion: pin route to model_id + model_instance_id to avoid ambiguous variant selection during swaps.

jane (Customer): What's the mitigation for us right now? We have clients failing assertion on vector length.

emma (Support): Short-term: set header X-Redwood-Batch-Size: 1 or add param batch_size=1 in the request to avoid server-side batching until we confirm. Also catch dimension error and fallback client-side to retry once.

sam (Eng Runtime): Agreed. Medium-term: I'll open a patch to make routing atomic with respect to model instance updates — router must only send to nodes whose loaded model_id+version exactly matches requested model. Also adding a server-side validation check: if resulting vector dims != expected, log as critical and return 409 with dimension_mismatch + model_variant reported.

mike (SRE): For observability improvements: adding a per-request debug tag that includes model_variant returned by the worker and model_selected by the router. Data pipeline: trace -> honeycomb fields: router.model_selected, worker.model_loaded, worker.model_variant, compute_ms. That will make triage faster.

emma (Support): I'm going to share mitigation steps with the customer: 1) set batch_size=1 2) add retry on 409 3) share request_ids for us to correlate if it happens again. Will also ask them to toggle verbose logging and keep timestamps.

jane (Customer): Doing that now. I set batch_size=1 and re-tested — no errors in 200 requests so far. Thanks.

sam (Eng Runtime): I'll schedule a hotfix to router logic and add the 409 dimension_mismatch metadata. I'll post PR and rollout ETA here.

mike (SRE): ETA for hotfix + deploy: 4 hours (can be expedited if needed). I'll coordinate canary.

ops-bot: Deploy triggered: PR #3421 -> canary on embed-pool-us-east. Link: https://ci.redwood.ai/changes/3421

sam (Eng Runtime): After canary completes we'll monitor traces for any router.model_selected != worker.model_loaded events. If none after 30m, will promote.

emma (Support): Marking customer update: recommend batching=1 for now; we'll follow up when patch is live. Adding to support ticket. :white_check_mark:

jane (Customer): Appreciate the quick turnaround. Please keep me posted on the permanent fix and if we should resume normal batching.

sam (Eng Runtime): Will do. Follow-ups: add dashboard card for embedding route that shows ratio of worker.model_loaded != router.model_selected, per-route p95/p99, and failed_dim_count. I'll post dashboard link when ready.

mike (SRE): Also adding an alert: failed_dim_count > 1 in 5m -> pager on-call.

emma (Support): Closing slack thread for now — will reopen if customer reports again.
